clue.text: Ridge outside Kent from which a light once shone

definitions.text: from which a light once shone

indicators.note: the ridge word is placed around the Kent letters, so it sits outside them

parts.note: a crest is the ridge or top of a hill
Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A hilltop beyond Kent where a beacon once burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts CREST around SE, splitting it after CRES. Kent is the county in England's South East corner, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset was an iron basket holding burning fuel, used historically as a beacon or torch.

clue.text: Gaming-house built by accountants in Ohio

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants
taken as written
O is a postal-style abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: A gambling hall constructed by number-crunchers in Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is an establishment for gambling, the meaning of gaming-house.

clue.text: Unpredictable fellow sheltering a deserter

indicators.note: the man's name gives shelter to the deserter, so it surrounds it

parts.note: Eric is any man's name, standing for a fellow
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A fickle man who hides a runaway soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is irregular and inconsistent, so it cannot be predicted.

clue.text: The northern city's 13 is art- artificially produced

indicators.note: the answer to 13 Down means a making-up or manufacture, so it tells you to remake these letters

explanation.surface: Claims that a northern city's story is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the answer to 13 Down, a word for a made-up story or a manufacturing: THE, N and CITYS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic materials are man-made by chemical processes rather than occurring naturally.

clue.text: Directions to swallow one pill before a game

indicators.note: before puts the pill word ahead of the directions piece

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

indicators.note: the compass letters swallow the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: E, N, N and S are compass directions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to take a pill ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' puts I inside ENNS, four compass points; 'Directions' reads like medical instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis is the indoor bat-and-ball sport also called ping-pong.

clue.text: Token is not real

explanation.surface: Something given as a token is not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal payment is a token sum in name only, and nominal also means existing in name but not in fact.

clue.text: Nothing new, a team being raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it upwards, so the team letters run backwards

parts.note: a cricket or football side is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Nothing fresh as a squad is formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nix is slang for nothing at all.

clue.text: Seamstress about to make a copy

parts.note: Mimi is the seamstress heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A dressmaker getting ready to duplicate a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi, the embroiderer in La Boheme, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate, reproducing someone's manner as a copy.

clue.text: Material bespoken for Edmund the actor's grandmother

indicators.note: bespoken, playing on spoken, says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Edmund Kean was a famous actor, so his grandmother is Nan Kean

explanation.surface: Cloth made to order for an old actor's grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bespoken' looks like tailoring, made to measure, but signals speech. Edmund Kean was a great English tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Mock duel about a singer in play

indicators.note: the scrambled duel letters go around the bird piece
mock as in mock-up, a false version, signals the letters of duel are rearranged

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A pretend sword fight round a vocalist in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' makes LUDE from DUEL, and 'about' puts it around A TIT. 'play' is freedom, not drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action, the sense of play as room to move.

clue.text: Vigorous fight to protect one's valuables

parts.note: vigorous means strong
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A hard battle to keep one's treasures safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox is a sturdy locked chest for keeping money and precious items secure.

clue.text: He painted a Scotsman — and in Paris too!

parts.note: mon is a Scots dialect form of man, so a Scotsman can be MON
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a Scot, and a Frenchman too, did some painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist artist known for his water lilies.

clue.text: Score for three clarinets originally used in Japanese drama

indicators.note: the two initial letters are put to work inside the drama word

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter of each of the words three and clarinets

explanation.surface: A musical score written for three clarinets in a Japanese play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks musical, but it means a cut or mark. 'used in' puts TC, from 'originally', inside NOH.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut a mark into it, which is a small nick or cut.

clue.text: Business-like company abandons product

indicators.note: the company abbreviation leaves the longer word, so it is removed from it

parts.note: a coefficient is a multiplying factor in a mathematical product

explanation.surface: A firm drops one of its products in a businesslike way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes CO away from the start of COEFFICIENT, a multiplier in a mathematical product.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone businesslike works in an organised, competent way without waste.

clue.text: Sailor involved in disagreement about a story

indicators.note: the sailor letters are wrapped up inside the disagreement word
the disagreement word goes round the letter a

parts.note: friction is conflict or disagreement
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman caught up in a quarrel over a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts AB inside FRICTION after F, and 'about' has FRICTION round A, after FRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabrication is an invented tale, a lie made up to deceive.

clue.text: Frivolous supporter at home in-broadcast

indicators.note: the supporter and home letters go inside the broadcast word

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so broadcast gives scattered
a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home

explanation.surface: A flighty fan staying in and watching a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts BRA and IN inside SCATTERED, after SCATTER. 'supporter' suggests a fan but is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is flighty and unable to concentrate, which is to say frivolous.

clue.text: Correction to notice about soldiers, intended to be announced

indicators.note: the notice word goes round the soldiers

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the intended word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Correcting a notice about troops, meant to be publicly read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be announced' changes MEANT to MENT, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to correct or improve a text, a revision.

clue.text: No man provides his home do we infer?

definitions.text: No man provides his home do we infer?

parts.words: No man provides his home do we infer?
parts.note: plays on Donne's line that no man is an island: a person whose home is on an island must be the exception

explanation.surface: Musing that nobody supplies his own home.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island'; the clue teases that someone living on one contradicts it.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander is a person who lives on an island, the home the clue hints at.

clue.text: Assurance finally deserts little creature with secret

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word deserts

parts.note: an elf is a small fairy creature
a confidence is a secret shared in trust

explanation.surface: Courage ultimately fails a tiny being who holds a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance in the sense of poise and belief in one's own abilities.

clue.text: By and by, a student might practise such thinking

parts.note: by and by means later on
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Eventually, a student may try creative problem solving.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate that British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means solving problems by indirect, creative approaches, named by Edward de Bono.

clue.text: It links the French king with seizure of power

parts.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power
le is French for the
R, for rex, means king

explanation.surface: A French monarch joins a takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupler is a device that connects two things, such as railway carriages.

clue.text: Fuel for one flying far from land say

indicators.note: say signals the bird's name is spoken and heard as a different word

parts.note: a petrel is a seabird that ranges far out over the ocean

explanation.surface: Fuel needed by a long-distance flyer far out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one flying' suggests an aircraft needing fuel, but it is a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is the British word for gasoline, a motor fuel.

clue.text: Song about troubled times in the plant

indicators.note: the song word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: troubled signals that the letters of times are disturbed

explanation.surface: Singing about hard times among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns TIMES into TEMIS, and 'about' puts ARIA round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs including wormwood and mugwort.

clue.text: Stale-smelling, like some grape-juice?

explanation.surface: A sniff of old wine juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Musty means smelling mouldy and stale; must is unfermented grape juice, so whimsically 'musty' would describe it.

clue.text: Italian leader interning English? The devil he is!

indicators.note: interning means holding inside, so the leader word encloses the English letter

parts.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian leader

explanation.surface: Mussolini locking up an Englishman, with an exclamation that he is a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deuce!' is an old exclamation in which the deuce means the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is an old euphemism for the Devil, as in 'what the deuce'.

clue.text: Game requiring many skills

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, so many
arts are skills, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: A sport that demands lots of different abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a big Roman numeral for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing small arrows at a board.

clue.text: Fraudulent sculptor?

parts.note: one who works with a carving tool, and also a slang word for a cheat or swindler

explanation.surface: A sculptor who is a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller is British slang for a swindler, while literally someone who uses a chisel, as a sculptor does.

clue.text: This hoax upset a dwarf

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the dwarf's name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Doc is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A trick that annoyed a small person.
explanation.walkthrough: COD is British slang for a hoax or spoof.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as a noun or adjective in British slang means a joke or a sham.

clue.text: Broadcast from journalist after the race

indicators.note: after places the journalist abbreviation behind the race word

parts.note: a relay is a team race
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A news report filed by a reporter after a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay a programme is to transmit it, so relayed means broadcast.

clue.text: Not sharp, but such a one's sure to be successful

definitions.text: such a one's sure to be successful

explanation.surface: Describing someone born talented, never pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural note is neither sharp nor flat; a natural is a person with innate talent, bound to succeed.
